newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Western Australia considers delaying gold royalty.
newsitem.headline: Western Australia considers delaying gold royalty.

text.p: Western Australia state resources minister Colin Barnett said on Friday he would consider delaying the introduction of the state government's controversial gold royalty.
"I met this morning with the gold industry and we discussed the royalty," Barnett told a media conference.
"I put a proposal to the industry about some delay to the royalty, about having a second component to be tied to the price of gold."
Asked how the industry had reacted to the proposal, he said: "Not all that well".

Miners in Western Australia, which produces about 70 percent of Australia's gold, were recently hit by the introduction of a 1.25 percent royalty on production, which increases to 2.5 percent in 1999/2000.

The gold industry has been under pressure after gold prices fell to a 12-year low earlier this month after an announcement by the Reserve Bank of Australia that it had sold 167 tonnes or two thirds of its reserves in the past six months.
